correctness.rationale: In Frobenius coordinates (H11,H22,sqrt(2) Re H12,sqrt(2) Im H12), the constant and the two nonconstant Fourier modes of the outer samples give the stated triangular block and two scalar singular directions. The triangular block has determinant sqrt(3)u exp(−u)>0. Its largest squared singular value exceeds 3u exp(−2u) everywhere; evaluating its characteristic polynomial at that number reduces the crossing to the strictly increasing h. I independently bounded exp(8/3) by rational Taylor sums (using geometric ratio at most 2/9 for the upper tail), which gives the bracket for h and the derivative bound on the pre-crossing trace-to-root-determinant quotient. Above the crossing the normalized block increases strictly in positive-definite order. At equality the determinant fixes the largest squared singular value to u, giving the threefold lower singular level and the sharp condition. Fourier inversion has the right conjugation sign; rank-at-most-one positive lifts give signal recovery up to phase, including the zero case. Independent high-precision bisection reproduced all stated digits.
residual_risks: The optimization is strictly within this one-parameter equal-output-weight family; it is not an arbitrary-geometry or nonlinear noise-optimality claim.
